verdict.summary: You can create a public OAuth app for customer workspaces. Linear does not document a provider review for normal OAuth use. Each workspace needs an admin to install an app-actor integration.
verdict.activeEffort: 3–6 hours, mostly building OAuth token storage and webhook verification
verdict.waitTime: No documented Linear provider review. A customer workspace approval process can add wait time.
verdict.mainGate: A workspace admin must complete app-actor installation. In a paid workspace that requires third-party app approval, the app must also be approved.

recommendation.text: Create a public OAuth application with actor=app. This lets each customer install the agent in their workspace. Actions then show as the app, not as the installing person.

sources.quote: Whether the app should be available only in the current workspace or installable by other workspaces.
Allowed values: private , public
when authenticating this way the user will instead authorize installing the app within the workspace, actions performed with the received OAuth token will come from the app itself.

scopeTiers.text: Read workspace data without making changes. This is the cheapest tier.

sources.quote: read - (Default) Read access for the user’s account. This scope will always be present.

scopeTiers.need: Read issues, projects, and other workspace data.

scopeTiers.text: Post agent replies with a narrow write permission. No Linear review is documented for this scope.

sources.quote: comments:create - Allows creating new issue comments
Once the user approves your application they will be redirected back to your application, with the OAuth authorization code in the URL params.

scopeTiers.text: Create and update issues with a focused permission. Do not request broad write unless targeted scopes cannot work.

sources.quote: issues:create - Allows creating and updating issues, and creating their attachments
write - Write access for the user’s account. If your application only needs to create comments, use a more targeted scope

scopeTiers.need: Create issues, update issues, and add issue attachments.

scopeTiers.text: Add special agent capabilities only when the product needs them. App actors cannot request admin.

sources.quote: app:assignable Allow the app to be assigned as a delegate on issues
app:mentionable Allow the app to be mentioned in issues, documents, and other editor surfaces
Note that integrations using the actor=app mode are not able to also request admin scope.

scopeTiers.need: Let users assign or mention the agent.

Authorization code

essentials.text: Use state and PKCE for OAuth callbacks. Verify webhooks from their raw body using Linear-Signature. Reject webhook events older than about one minute.

sources.quote: Linear supports the PKCE flow . To use this flow, you’ll need to include two additional parameters as part of your /authorize request:
This header contains a hex-encoded HMAC-SHA256 signature of the raw body contents, signed using the webhook’s signing secret.
We recommend that you verify it’s within a minute of the time your system sees it to guard against replay attacks.

detail.text: Create a dedicated Linear workspace for the OAuth app. Limit workspace administrators because every administrator can access the app.

sources.quote: It is highly recommended you create a workspace for the purpose of managing the OAuth2 Application, as each admin user will have access.

detail.text: Open Settings, Administration, then API. Create an OAuth application and set distribution to public. Copy the client ID and secret into secure server-side storage.

sources.quote: Create and manage webhooks and OAuth applications in _Settings > Administration > API._ Admin permissions in your workspace are necessary to view this page.
Allowed values: private , public

detail.text: Add your HTTPS OAuth callback URL in the app settings. Use that exact URL in authorization and token exchange requests.

sources.quote: Format: absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL

redirect_uri

detail.text: Use app actor mode for autonomous actions. Include actor=app in every authorization URL used for an agent installation. Request only the scopes the product needs. Include state and PKCE values generated for each installation attempt.

sources.quote: To enable the actor authorization, add actor=app parameter to your OAuth authorization URL .

state 
 (optional, recommended ) Prevents CSRF attacks and should always be supplied.

detail.text: Exchange the authorization code at the token endpoint. Encrypt credentials at rest. Store the workspace-specific app ID beside each credential record. Refresh once per installation at a time.

sources.quote: POST https://api.linear.app/oauth/token HTTP/1.1 Pass parameters in body as URL-encoded form submission
Your app will have a unique ID for each workspace it is installed within
Save the returned credentials together and coordinate refreshes across processes sharing an authorization.

steps.title: Prepare webhook verification

detail.text: Use the unmodified request body for HMAC verification. Reject events outside a one-minute receipt window.

sources.quote: It’s strongly recommended to use raw request body rather than restringifying a parsed JSON body
We recommend that you verify it’s within a minute of the time your system sees it to guard against replay attacks.

detail.text: Install the public app in a test workspace as its administrator. Confirm issue changes show the app as the actor.

sources.quote: Because this will be installed with a workspace scope admin permissions are required to complete the installation.
In this mode, all mutations such as creating issues, comments, and status changes will be performed by the app.

detail.text: Configure a public HTTPS webhook endpoint. Enable webhooks and select Agent session events. Test with a request capture service before production.

sources.quote: In the configuration, enable webhooks and make sure to select Agent session events at the bottom.
It’s available in a publicly accessible HTTPS, non-localhost URL
requestbin.com is a great tool for testing webhooks

detail.text: Test a refresh, then save both returned tokens atomically. Test disconnect by calling the revocation endpoint with the stored token.

sources.quote: Each refresh token expires 30 days after issuance. A successful refresh returns a new access token and refresh token, with a new 30-day refresh-token lifetime.
To revoke a user’s access, call the revocation endpoint and include the token to be revoked in the token form field of the request body.

detail.text: No Linear production review is documented for normal OAuth scopes, so do not treat provider review as a launch gate. Ask each customer whether its workspace requires third-party app approval.

sources.quote: Once the user approves your application they will be redirected back to your application, with the OAuth authorization code in the URL params.
Requiring approval for third-party applications ensures that the people with permission to manage apps control which applications can access the workspace and its data.

detail.text: Subscribe to PermissionChange webhooks. Check the stored workspace identity before every action. Stop actions immediately after access changes or revocation.

sources.quote: The team access available to your app can be changed or revoked at any time by workspace admins.
a PermissionChange webhook will be sent when access changes occur.

detail.text: Clearly identify the product as an agent so people do not mistake it for a person. Show progress for long actions. Let people stop it immediately. Keep final responsibility with a person.

sources.quote: The agent must signal its identity clearly so that it can never be mistaken for a person.
Human responsibility must remain final even when an agent carries out tasks.

gotchas.text: Do not request admin with actor=app. Linear disallows that scope combination.

sources.quote: Note that integrations using the actor=app mode are not able to also request admin scope.

gotchas.text: Repeating installation does not add scopes. Request all old and new scopes with the update mechanism.

sources.quote: Request the complete scope set: all existing scopes plus any scopes being added.
Repeating the ordinary installation flow without update_scopes_on_existing_token=true does not update an existing installation.

gotchas.text: Removing scopes requires revocation and a new authorization. An ordinary scope update cannot reduce access.

sources.quote: To remove scopes, revoke the existing authorization and authorize again with the reduced scope set.

gotchas.text: API calls do not extend token lifetimes. Refresh tokens rotate, so stale tokens can break automation.

sources.quote: API requests do not extend either lifetime.
Each refresh token expires 30 days after issuance. A successful refresh returns a new access token and refresh token, with a new 30-day refresh-token lifetime.

gotchas.text: Customer workspaces can require their own approval even though Linear does not review your OAuth app.

sources.quote: Workspace owners in Enterprise workspaces—and workspace admins in all other paid workspaces—will receive an email and an in-app notification when an application has been requested for approval.

log.name: read
detail: Linear recommends OAuth2 for applications integrating with Linear. | quote: "Linear supports OAuth2 authentication, which is recommended if you’re building applications to integrate with Linear."
Create an OAuth2 Application and configure its redirect callback URLs. | quote: "Create a new OAuth2 Application and configure the redirect callback URLs to your application."

A dedicated workspace is highly recommended because each admin user can access the OAuth2 Application. | quote: "It is highly recommended you create a workspace for the purpose of managing the OAuth2 Application, as each admin user will have access."
All OAuth2 applications migrated to the new refresh-token system on April 1, 2026. | quote: "All OAuth2 applications were migrated to the new refresh token system on April 1, 2026."
The authorization endpoint is `https://linear.app/oauth/authorize`. | quote: "GET https://linear.app/oauth/authorize HTTP/1.1"
Authorization requests require `client_id`, `redirect_uri`, `response_type=code`, and `scope`. | quote: "client_id \n (required) Client ID provided when you create the OAuth2 Application"
The redirect URI is required during authorization and must be the configured callback URI. | quote: "redirect_uri \n (required) Redirect URI"
The authorization-code response type is required. | quote: "response_type=code \n (required) Expected response type"

The default `read` scope always appears; available scopes include `write`, `issues:create`, `comments:create`, `timeSchedule:write`, and `admin`. | quote: "read - (Default) Read access for the user’s account. This scope will always be present."

The `admin` scope grants full admin-level endpoint access and should only be requested when absolutely necessary. | quote: "admin - Full access to admin level endpoints. You should never ask for this permission unless it’s absolutely needed"
`state` is optional but recommended to prevent CSRF attacks. | quote: "state \n (optional, recommended ) Prevents CSRF attacks and should always be supplied."
The consent prompt can be forced on every authorization by using `prompt=consent`. | quote: "The consent screen is displayed every time, even if all scopes were previously granted."

The `actor` parameter selects whether resources are created as the authorizing user or the application; the default is `user`. | quote: "user - (Default) Resources are created as the user who authorized the application."

After approval, Linear redirects to the configured URL with an authorization code; returned `state` must match the original value. | quote: "Any state parameter you specified in step 2 will also be returned in the URL params and must match the value specified in step 2."

Linear supports PKCE using required `code_challenge` and `code_challenge_method` authorization parameters; the method is `plain` or `S256`. | quote: "Linear supports the PKCE flow . To use this flow, you’ll need to include two additional parameters as part of your /authorize request:"

The token endpoint is `https://api.linear.app/oauth/token`, and requests use URL-encoded form data with the specified content type. | quote: "POST https://api.linear.app/oauth/token HTTP/1.1 Pass parameters in body as URL-encoded form submission"

Authorization-code token exchange requires `code`, the same `redirect_uri`, `client_id`, `client_secret`, and `grant_type=authorization_code`. | quote: "redirect_uri \n (required) Same redirect URI which you used in the previous step"

With PKCE, `code_verifier` is required and `client_secret` is optional. | quote: "code_verifier \n (required) The code verifier for the PKCE request that you originally generated before the authorization request"

Authorization-code access tokens last 24 hours by default and are renewed by exchanging a refresh token for a new token pair. | quote: "Authorization code
 user or app 
 24 hours by default
 Exchange the refresh token for a new token pair."

Each refresh token expires 30 days after issuance; successful refresh rotates both tokens and starts a new 30-day refresh-token lifetime. | quote: "Each refresh token expires 30 days after issuance. A successful refresh returns a new access token and refresh token, with a new 30-day refresh-token lifetime."

log.name: read
detail: OAuth actor authorization changes the actor from the authenticating user to the app, useful for agents and service accounts. | quote: "when authenticating this way the user will instead authorize installing the app within the workspace, actions performed with the received OAuth token will come from the app itself."

Enable app-actor authorization by adding the `actor=app` parameter to the OAuth authorization URL. | quote: "To enable the actor authorization, add actor=app parameter to your OAuth authorization URL ."
The actor setting is tied to the authorization and access token. | quote: "The setting is tied to the authorization and its access token."

In app-actor mode, mutations such as issue creation, comments, and status changes are performed by the app. | quote: "In this mode, all mutations such as creating issues, comments, and status changes will be performed by the app."

Updating scopes for authorization-code installations requires the complete scope set and is subject to permission and team-access checks. | quote: "Request the complete scope set: all existing scopes plus any scopes being added. The update is subject to permission and team-access checks."

Repeating the ordinary installation flow does not update an existing installation’s scopes. | quote: "Repeating the ordinary installation flow without update_scopes_on_existing_token=true does not update an existing installation."

Removing scopes requires revoking the existing authorization and authorizing again with the reduced scope set. | quote: "To remove scopes, revoke the existing authorization and authorize again with the reduced scope set."

For client credentials, changing scopes revokes existing app-actor tokens for the app in the workspace. | quote: "Adding or removing scopes revokes existing app-actor tokens for that app in the workspace."

Processes sharing an app must use the same scope set to avoid invalidating one another’s tokens. | quote: "Processes sharing the app must use the same scope set to avoid invalidating each other’s tokens."

App actions can display an optional custom user name and avatar in `User (via Application)` format. | quote: "You can also add an optional user name and avatar to go with the application to have it rendered in User (via Application) format."

The deprecated `actor=application` mode may continue to be used by existing apps. | quote: "actor=application as a mode – this was deprecated in favor of the behavior in actor=app . If your app already uses this option then you can continue to do so."

log.name: read
detail: Agents can be built for internal workspace use or distributed to other organizations. | quote: "You can build agents for internal use within your own workspace or for distribution to other organizations."
Agents can be submitted to Linear’s integration directory for distribution. | quote: "To make your agent available to other workspaces, submit your agent to Linear’s integration directory."
Developing agents in Linear is free. | quote: "It does not cost anything to develop agents in Linear."
Agents installed in a workspace are not billable users. | quote: "Additionally, agents installed in your workspace do not count as billable users."
Agents are configured as applications with webhooks and Agent session events enabled. | quote: "Create a new Application and configure the settings as you would for a standard OAuth application."
Agent session events should be selected to receive relevant user events. | quote: "In the configuration, enable webhooks and make sure to select Agent session events at the bottom."

Agent installations use OAuth with the `actor=app` parameter. | quote: "In the OAuth authorization url add the actor=app parameter to switch to an app installation rather than requesting authentication as the installing user."
Workspace-scope installation requires admin permissions. | quote: "Because this will be installed with a workspace scope admin permissions are required to complete the installation."

`actor=app` supersedes `actor=application` for agent, app, and service account use cases. | quote: "This new actor type supersedes any references to actor=application and can be used for all agent, app, and service account use-cases."
Assignability and mentionability are optional OAuth scopes. | quote: "the ability to mention and assign your agent is optional and must be requested through the use of two new additional scopes"
The `app:assignable` scope allows assignment as an issue delegate. | quote: "app:assignable Allow the app to be assigned as a delegate on issues"
The `app:mentionable` scope allows mentions across supported editor surfaces. | quote: "app:mentionable Allow the app to be mentioned in issues, documents, and other editor surfaces"

Assigning an issue makes the agent the delegate rather than the assignee. | quote: "Assigning an issue to your app now sets it as the delegate , not the assignee —so humans maintain ownership while agents act on their behalf."
Agents cannot be project members or project leads, even with assignability. | quote: "Agents cannot be added as project members or set as project leads, even with the app:assignable scope."
Customer data access requires customer scopes. | quote: "The ability to access customer-related entities in your workspace for your agent must be requested through scopes:"
The `customer:read` scope permits reading customer data. | quote: "customer:read Allow the app to read customer data in the workspace"
The `customer:write` scope permits reading and writing customer data. | quote: "customer:write Allow the app to read and write customer data in the workspace"
Initiative data access requires initiative scopes. | quote: "The ability to access initiative-related entities in your workspace for your agent must be requested through scopes:"
The `initiative:read` scope permits reading initiative data. | quote: "initiative:read Allow the app to read initiative data in the workspace"
The `initiative:write` scope permits reading and writing initiative data. | quote: "initiative:write Allow the app to read and write initiative data in the workspace"

detail: OAuth app manifests define a Linear OAuth app as structured data instead of requiring manual form entry. | quote: "OAuth app manifests let developers define a Linear OAuth app as structured data instead of filling the form manually."
URL parameters can directly pre-populate the OAuth application creation page. | quote: "Use URL parameters when you want to send someone directly to a pre-filled app setup page."
The direct create URL is the workspace-agnostic application creation form at `https://linear.app/settings/api/applications/new`. | quote: "https://linear.app/settings/api/applications/new"

A JSON manifest can be passed directly to the create page through one `manifest` query parameter. | quote: "A JSON manifest can be passed to the create page through a single manifest query parameter."

The manifest query parameter is useful for opening the app creation page with an existing JSON configuration applied. | quote: "This is useful when the configuration already exists as JSON and you want to open the app creation page with that manifest applied directly."

Distribution supports private apps limited to the current workspace and public apps installable by other workspaces. | quote: "Whether the app should be available only in the current workspace or installable by other workspaces."
Distribution accepts `private` or `public`, with `private` as the default. | quote: "Allowed values: private , public"

The JSON manifest likewise distinguishes between private-to-one-workspace and publicly installable applications. | quote: "Whether the application is private to one workspace or publicly installable."

log.name: read
detail: API requests use three HTTP response headers to track global rate limits. | quote: "To make it easier to keep track and avoid going over the limits, there are 3 HTTP response headers we send back on each request."
`X-RateLimit-Requests-Limit` is the global hourly request limit. | quote: "X-RateLimit-Requests-Limit The maximum number of API requests you’re permitted to make per hour."
`X-RateLimit-Requests-Remaining` reports requests left in the current window. | quote: "X-RateLimit-Requests-Remaining The number of API requests remaining in the current rate limit window."
`X-RateLimit-Requests-Reset` reports the UTC epoch-millisecond reset time. | quote: "X-RateLimit-Requests-Reset The time at which the current rate limit window resets in UTC epoch milliseconds ."

API keys allow up to 2,500 requests per hour, shared by the authenticated user across API keys. | quote: "When authenticated using an API key you can make up to 2,500 requests per hour . Requests are associated with the authenticated user"
OAuth apps allow 5,000 requests per hour per user or app user. | quote: "OAuth App 5,000 User (or App User) 1 hour"
Unauthenticated requests allow 600 requests per hour per originating IP address. | quote: "Unauthenticated 600 IP Address 1 hour"

Query- and mutation-specific limits can be lower than the global limit, with endpoint-specific windows. | quote: "Some queries and mutations have individual request rate limits that are lower than the global request limit."
Endpoint-specific limits include four additional headers. | quote: "We will also send these extra headers:"

`X-RateLimit-Endpoint-Requests-Limit` reports the endpoint request limit. | quote: "X-RateLimit-Endpoint-Requests-Limit The maximum number of API requests you’re permitted to make to this endpoint in a rate limit window."

`X-RateLimit-Endpoint-Requests-Remaining` reports remaining endpoint requests. | quote: "X-RateLimit-Endpoint-Requests-Remaining The number of API requests remaining in the current rate limit window."

`X-RateLimit-Endpoint-Requests-Reset` reports the endpoint window reset time in UTC epoch milliseconds. | quote: "X-RateLimit-Endpoint-Requests-Reset The time at which the current rate limit window resets in UTC epoch milliseconds ."
`X-RateLimit-Endpoint-Name` identifies the rate-limited endpoint. | quote: "X-RateLimit-Endpoint-Name The name of the endpoint that was rate limited."
Complexity limits include four response headers. | quote: "To make it easier to keep track and avoid going over the limits, there are 4 HTTP response headers we send back on each request."
`X-Complexity` reports query complexity. | quote: "X-Complexity The complexity of the query."
`X-RateLimit-Complexity-Limit` reports the hourly complexity-point limit. | quote: "X-RateLimit-Complexity-Limit The maximum number of API complexity points you’re permitted to request per hour."

`X-RateLimit-Complexity-Remaining` reports remaining complexity points. | quote: "X-RateLimit-Complexity-Remaining The number of points of API request complexity remaining in the current rate limit window."

`X-RateLimit-Complexity-Reset` reports the complexity-window reset time in UTC epoch milliseconds. | quote: "X-RateLimit-Complexity-Reset The time at which the current rate limit window resets in UTC epoch milliseconds ."

API keys allow 3,000,000 complexity points per hour, shared by the authenticated user across API keys. | quote: "Requests authenticated using an API key can request up to 3,000,000 points per hour . Requests are associated with the authenticated user"
OAuth apps allow 2,000,000 complexity points per hour per user or app user. | quote: "OAuth app 2,000,000 User (or App User) 1 hour"

detail: Webhook consumers must use a publicly accessible HTTPS URL that is not localhost. | quote: "It’s available in a publicly accessible HTTPS, non-localhost URL"
Webhook endpoints must respond to Linear’s POST request with HTTP 200. | quote: "It will respond to the Linear Webhook push (HTTP POST request) with a HTTP 200 (“OK”) response"

Failed deliveries are retried up to three times with delays of one minute, one hour, and six hours. | quote: "the push will be retried a maximum of 3 times. A backoff delay is used: the attempt will be retried after 1 minute, 1 hour, and finally after 6 hours."

Linear may disable a webhook that remains unresponsive, requiring manual re-enablement. | quote: "If the webhook URL continues to be unresponsive the webhook might be disabled by Linear, and must be re-enabled again manually."
RequestBin is suggested for testing webhook endpoints. | quote: "requestbin.com is a great tool for testing webhooks"

Webhooks can be configured through Linear API settings after creating a consumer endpoint. | quote: "Once your consumer is ready to receive updates, you can enable it for your Linear team. You can configure webhooks in Linear from API settings."
Webhook creation requires specifying an endpoint URL, and the webhook is enabled by default after successful creation. | quote: "That’s it! Your webhook is now ready to use and enabled by default."

Each webhook request includes a `Linear-Signature` header containing an HMAC-SHA256 signature of the raw body. | quote: "This header contains a hex-encoded HMAC-SHA256 signature of the raw body contents, signed using the webhook’s signing secret."
The signing secret is available on the webhook detail page. | quote: "You can find the signing secret on the webhook’s detail page."

Signature verification should compute an HMAC over the raw request body and compare it with the `Linear-Signature` header. | quote: "To verify the webhook, you need to compute the signature of the request body using the webhook’s signing secret and compare it against the Linear-Signature header."

Verification should use the raw body rather than re-stringifying parsed JSON. | quote: "It’s strongly recommended to use raw request body rather than restringifying a parsed JSON body, otherwise the signature may differ."

The request body’s `webhookTimestamp` should be checked to prevent replay attacks. | quote: "We recommend that you verify it’s within a minute of the time your system sees it to guard against replay attacks."

Invalid signatures and stale timestamps should be rejected with HTTP 401 in the provided Express example. | quote: "if (!verifySignature(req.get(\"linear-signature\"), req.rawBody)) { return res.sendStatus(401); }"
The example rejects webhook timestamps older or newer than 60 seconds. | quote: "if (Math.abs(Date.now() - req.body.webhookTimestamp) > 60 * 1000) {"
Signature comparison should use a timing-safe comparison. | quote: "return crypto.timingSafeEqual(computedSignature, headerSignature);"
The source IP address can also be checked as an additional security measure. | quote: "In addition to verifying the signature, you can check the source IP address."
A successful verified webhook should return HTTP 200; server errors should return HTTP 500 so Linear retries delivery. | quote: "return res.sendStatus(500);"

log.name: read
detail: Page date: Apr 1, 2026 | quote: "Apr 1, 2026"
Linear refresh failures commonly return HTTP 400 with OAuth error `invalid_grant`. | quote: "Common HTTP status: 400

The error means the stored refresh token cannot mint a new access token, and retrying the same request will continue failing. | quote: "the refresh token you have stored can’t be used to mint a new access token. Retrying the same request will keep failing"

Root causes include invalid, expired, revoked, or stale refresh tokens after rotation. | quote: "This happens because the token is invalid, expired, revoked, or you’re using a stale token after rotation."

Linear rotates refresh tokens; exchanging one invalidates the previous access and refresh tokens. | quote: "when a refresh token is exchanged, the previous access and refresh tokens are invalidated and new tokens are returned."

Concurrent refreshes can cause one process to overwrite the current refresh token with a stale one. | quote: "one process stores the “new” refresh token, another process overwrites it with the stale one, and suddenly every refresh starts failing."
Linear access tokens expire in 24 hours when refresh tokens are enabled. | quote: "Linear access tokens expire in 24 hours when refresh tokens are enabled."

An inactive, expired refresh token causes `invalid_grant` and requires re-authorization. | quote: "if the refresh token itself has expired due to inactivity, Linear returns invalid_grant and requires re-authorization."
Removing or revoking the app invalidates all associated tokens. | quote: "Linear immediately invalidates all associated tokens."

Refresh requests may be rejected because the token was already rotated, retried after a duplicate-refresh grace period, or sent with incorrect client credentials. | quote: "The refresh token is stale because it was already rotated"
Scope or app-configuration changes can invalidate existing refresh tokens and require re-authorization. | quote: "existing refresh tokens may become invalid and require re-authorization."

Incorrect client credentials can result from secret rotation, wrong workspace credentials, or environment-variable errors. | quote: "Using incorrect client_id or client_secret when refreshing tokens will result in invalid_grant errors."
Simultaneous refreshes by multiple workers create a race in which a worker uses a stale token. | quote: "Worker B refreshes with the now-stale token and gets invalid_grant"

Security heuristics may revoke tokens for unusual access patterns, suspicious activity, rate-limit violations, or detected compromise. | quote: "Linear may revoke refresh tokens based on security heuristics or policy changes."

Persist every new `refresh_token` returned by Linear and use it for the next refresh. | quote: "If Linear returns a new refresh_token on refresh, always persist it and use that value for the next refresh."
Refresh requests should use `grant_type=refresh_token`, form encoding, appropriate client authentication, and Linear’s token endpoint. | quote: "grant_type=refresh_token

Only one refresh should run per connection; other requests should wait for the in-flight refresh. | quote: "Only one refresh can run for a given connection at a time (distributed lock or single-flight)"
Token state updates should atomically include access token, refresh token, and expiration time. | quote: "Updates to (access_token, refresh_token, expires_at) happen atomically"

Treat persistent `invalid_grant` as terminal after ruling out rotation and credential issues; trigger re-authentication instead of repeatedly retrying. | quote: "treat invalid_grant as a terminal state for that connection."

The production playbook is to retry once, mark the connection as needing re-authentication after a second failure, pause background syncs, and ask the user to reconnect. | quote: "If it fails again, mark the connection as “needs re-auth”"
